records.text: On June 18, Charlie Kirk opposed Benjamin Netanyahu's push for more U.S. action in Iran at the White House and prevailed in keeping the operation limited.
records.speaker: Candace Owens

appearances.snippet: That is when Charlie (Charlie Kirk) goes into the White House. We have confirmed those dates thanks to Bret Weinstein. ... Goes into the White House and he is arguing for us not to get involved in Israel's war with Iran. ... And he is debating very powerful Zionist lobbies—Zionist lobbyists—who are there to argue on behalf of Bibi (Benjamin Netanyahu). ... And Charlie (Charlie Kirk) emerges the temporary winner of that. Trump (Donald Trump) moves to limit his involvement.

Well, I can now confirm that the date that Charlie (Charlie Kirk) went to the White House, went to the White House and went up. ... like toe-to-toe with Bibi (Benjamin Netanyahu)'s and his thugs who wanted more action in Iran and he won was on June 18th. ... keep this as a limited operation.

verification.notes: Washington Post reporting confirms Kirk opposed deeper U.S. involvement in Iran and visited Trump at the White House, but reports the visit as June 19 rather than June 18. The later U.S. operation was limited to Iranian nuclear targets, but no public record establishes that Kirk confronted Netanyahu or his representatives there, prevailed in a contest with them, or caused the operation's limited scope.

records.text: Charlie Kirk advocated to President Trump against war with Iran, and Israel was expected to ask the United States to return to war after Operation Midnight Hammer.
records.speaker: Joe Kent

appearances.snippet: And again, we know Charlie was advocating to President Trump against this war with Iran. And we knew at the end of the 12-day war, at the end of Midnight Hammer, that the Israelis were going to come back and ask us to go back to war.

verification.notes: Kent's firsthand Tucker Carlson account says Kirk urged him in the West Wing to stop a war with Iran. The full interview also records Kent's account that Israeli officials had communicated a regime-change goal and that U.S. skeptics expected Israel to seek renewed U.S. action after Midnight Hammer. These are direct insider assertions but lack released contemporaneous records, so confidence is medium.
